classificationKey.a: Outdated behavior or test fixture; source or contract evidence cited.
classificationKey.b: Real implementation or harness bug; original assertions retained.
classificationKey.c: Timing, ordering, or cancellation-ownership failure; deterministic barriers or explicit cancellation. Unreproduced timeout causes remain identified as unknown.

counting: 51 baseline failing leaf tests or failed module loads, plus 28 additionally exposed tests, for 79 classified records. Two failing parent containers duplicate their failed subtests and are not classified again. Additional records cover the restored agent-tools assertion, Node startup readiness, durable-clock time limits, OAuth cancellation ownership, aborted fake-model uploads, run-stream completion, an unreproduced native fixture startup exit, and a malformed release-note heading caught by CI. Unknown original causes remain explicit. A later full parity run exposed 20 synthetic Python case failures from two truncated cached native modules; one cache-integrity guard addresses all 20 without changing their assertions.

tests.test: container
tests.reason: The fixture migrated from wrangler dev to unstable_dev, whose programmatic API disables containers by default. The declared Durable Object therefore had no ctx.container and every native operation failed. The nested prompt fixture also used a tenant token where src requires the agent token, and inspected obsolete request.status instead of request.state. The first required native CI run then reached Docker successfully but both nested codemode calls failed because enabledToolsImpl unconditionally disabled the registered computer tool even when a native provider binding was configured.
evidence: wrangler@4.157.0: unstable_dev sets enableContainers from experimental.enableContainers, default false
tests.change: Enable declared native containers in unstable_dev and use agent credentials and source-defined request state for nested execution. Retain every exec/read/write/parse/network/snapshot assertion. Per coordinator instruction, explicitly skip this native suite on unsupported Sprite hosts or unavailable local Docker/Buildx; WORKERS_REQUIRE_DOCKER=1 in CI converts host unavailability to a failure. No proxy image, Docker wrapper, or runtime changes remain. Select the native computer tool only when COMPUTER_CONTAINERS or COMPUTER_SANDBOXES is configured and codeMode is enabled. Extract the actual selector into the existing pure file-tool-selection module and retain every native integration assertion.

tests.test: a run stops at its time limit before its next model request
tests.reason: The copied test times a synchronous codemode busy loop with Date.now. Durable QuickJS uses a deterministic virtual clock initialized at start and advanced only when a host result is delivered. The loop cannot represent elapsed wall time and instead depends on the interrupt budget; a clean lifecycle rerun timed out after 30 seconds.
tests.change: Use an HTTP tool-entry barrier, wait for the same one-second run limit through the fixture wall-clock operation, then release the tool. Retain the exact stopped/error, one-model-response, and first-tool history assertions. No timeout increase; replace the old 1500ms busy loop with a 1000ms interval after observed tool entry.

tests.test: a run's event stream follows it to its end, and picks up after Last-Event-ID without a gap or a repeat
tests.reason: Workers ended live and replayed run streams only with a physical WebSocket close. The SDK could keep the readable stream open while waiting for that handshake even after the terminal response arrived. A phase-timed run spent 10603ms closing the resumed stream and another 8444ms waiting for the completed-run replay before the 30s test timeout. The existing protocol closed frame tells the client to end immediately.
tests.change: Send the protocol closed marker after the terminal response and before socket.close in both live and replay paths. Retain every cursor/order/no-gap/final-response assertion, assert terminal response before the marker for both paths, and replace 300/800ms provider delays with connection-ready barriers. No framework deadline increase.

previousAttempt.reason: Diagnostic source edits during execution changed suiteHash; frozen-source rerun required.

dockerHostPolicy.sprite: Explicit native-suite skip with unsupported-host reason, as directed by coordinator.
dockerHostPolicy.ci: .github/workflows/workers-tests.yml runs full integration with Docker/Buildx preflight and WORKERS_REQUIRE_DOCKER=1; unavailable Docker fails rather than skips.

invocationCorrections: Run group jobs with bash -c: login-shell .bash_logout plus errexit changed successful npm exits into failures. All groups are verified with captured command exit codes.
The initial full-parity local inventory lacked dependencies. Reused the existing main-worktree node_modules cache for local report assembly; all actual contract execution remains on Sprites.
CI helper tests need Git metadata. The first docs validation used the normal Sprite archive without .git; the corrected command creates and removes a temporary Git repository on the Sprite.

Final suite wrapper used bash -lc despite the earlier correction. npm unit/integration and both typechecks write independent exit files; use those and the complete TAP counts. The login-shell wrapper exit is recorded separately and is not a suite failure. No tests were rerun to hide it.

The first final-parity launcher lacked sandbox permission for the Sprites CLI organization-selection file and launched no tests. The authorized invocation runs the same npm run parity command on Sprites.

docs.command: npm run docs; node --experimental-strip-types --test --test-name-pattern="llms.txt" tests/docs.test.ts; exact CI docs test command

spriteRunner.wrapperIssue: The login-shell logout returned 1 after every npm command completed with exit 0. No suite was rerun.

realBugs.issue: Creation accepted null keyScope; clearing a scope also needed removal before stored-configuration revalidation.
Pure tool transport imports eagerly loaded runtime-only storage and Cloudflare modules; the JSON import also lacked its required type attribute.
The default media integration fixture omitted its fake model credentials.
Programmatic Wrangler disabled declared native containers, and tool selection hid the native computer tool even with configured bindings. Native tests require a Docker-capable host.
Cancelling an incomplete fake-model HTTP upload leaked its expected ECONNRESET rejection into the test runner.
Completed Workers run streams waited for the physical WebSocket close handshake instead of sending the existing protocol close marker.
An existing Workers release-note fragment omitted the section heading required by the release-note parser.

The Python dependency cache trusted its ready marker while two native wheel files were truncated, causing SIGBUS before 20 contract cases could report results. Validate installed wheel sizes and hashes before reusing the cache. The external truncation cause is unknown.
